goal: Finish the demo panel: make the counters account for every node in every beat, and make the panel fit a narrow viewport
context: Round 0007 was a large success and I am not asking you to revisit any of it. Verified against the live page: the type floor is now 12px with zero elements below it, the caption is 15px and the largest visible body text, the terminal shows a complete object with one key per line and no ellipsis in all three beats, the panel grew from 1152x385 to 1152x523 and its ratio from 3.0 to 2.2, the graph no longer nests the gate inside the task it blocks, the lifecycle row now reads as a labelled stepper whose steps are clickable, and the log accumulates rows 1 to 2 to 3 with labelled action, actor and node columns before restarting cleanly. Beats measure 9.4s, 9.4s and 11.2s over a 30s loop, and the pause control genuinely holds: 15 seconds of sampling produced a single distinct state, the button toggles its pressed state, and resuming advances correctly. I also checked the demo against the real CLI on a scratch project and it is honest: freshly_claimed, newly_ready and the log actions take, task.submit and task.accept all match the real output exactly. So this round is only about the three things left, and the first one is the important one. In the accept beat the counter pills read 1 ready, 1 blocked, 1 open gates, which sums to three, while the graph shows four nodes with one marked done. I measured all three beats: take sums to 4 and matches the graph, submit sums to 4 and matches, accept sums to 3 against a graph of 4. The node that disappears from the count is the done one, and it disappears in exactly the beat whose caption is teaching that acceptance is what satisfies the blocker, so a reader who counts sees the arithmetic break at the moment the point is being made. The real climier status summary carries a done counter, so the honest fix is to count it. Separately, the panel is 1089px tall at 390x844, which is 1.29 viewport heights, and 923px at 768x900. The 390 header alone is 152px because the framing command, the three pills and the rev counter with its two controls wrap onto three rows; the body grid below it is 830px and the stepper 105px. And on the 390 layout each card pushes its status pill to the far right of a full-width row, leaving a wide empty run between the node title and its pill.

targets.selector: figure.landing-panel header ul, the counter pills, in the accept beat
targets.intent: Make every beat's counters account for every node drawn in the graph. The accept beat must count the done node as well, so that take, submit and accept all sum to the four nodes on screen. Use the same counter vocabulary the real status summary uses, and keep the existing pill styling, ordering and accent treatment.
targets.notes: I verified the arithmetic per beat: take in progress 1 + blocked 2 + open 1 equals 4 nodes and is correct; submit submitted 1 + blocked 2 + open 1 equals 4 and is correct; accept done 1 + ready 1 + blocked 1 + open 1 equals 4 in the graph but the pills only sum to 3. Do not change the take or submit counters, they are right.

targets.intent: Bring the panel down to roughly one viewport height at 390 without losing any of the legibility the last round won. The two places with room to give are the header, which currently takes three rows at 390, and the vertical rhythm between the four graph cards. The framing command must stay visible, the caption must stay at its current size, the type floor of 12px is absolute, and nothing may be dropped, collapsed behind a control, or made to require a tap to read.
targets.notes: Current numbers at 390x844: header 152px, body grid 830px, stepper 105px, total 1089px. Target is about 860px or less at 390. At 768x900 the panel is 923px, so a modest tightening there is welcome too. Do not solve this by hiding the log or the terminal at narrow widths; the whole point of the panel is that a first-time visitor can read one complete example.

targets.intent: Tighten the relationship between each node's title and its status pill so they read as one unit instead of two ends of a wide empty row, and stop the rev counter and its two controls from sitting alone on their own right-aligned row if the header can be organised better.
